text:
Alex: Heads up — noticed a big jump in GPU spend for us starting ~03:10 UTC, looks like autoscaler launched a batch of nodes in us-west1.
cloud-cost-bot: ALERT: sudden spend anomaly detected: +420% GPU-hour usage in project/redwood-prod (03:12 UTC). Invoice estimate attached.
Priya: wow, link to the estimate?
Jamal: pulling billing export now, running a quick BQ query to see instance types.
Jamal: ```SELECT resource.labels.machine_type, SUM(cost) as cost FROM billing_export WHERE project = 'redwood-prod' AND invoice_period_start >= '2026-03-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY cost DESC LIMIT 10;```
Jamal: results: `n1-standard-8+NVIDIA_A100` = $18k, `n2-highmem-16+NVIDIA_A10G` = $1.2k.
Emily: That smells like the autoscaler template picked A100 family instead of A10G. Iirc the terraform module had a var default that sneaked in after the provider upgrade.
Alex: Is this a config drift or a typo in the launch template?
Ogden: Oncall now. I can scale the pool down while we investigate. Which pool is it?
Priya: pool name `gpu-spot-us-west1-autoscale`. Should be A10G preemptible for inference, but the node pool definition shows `accelerator_type: A100` in the generated instance-template.
Emily: snippets from the TF output: ```resource "google_compute_instance_template" "gpu" { name = "gpu-template-${var.env} " guest_accelerator { type = var.gpu_type count = var.gpu_count } }```
Var file shows `gpu_type = "NVIDIA_A100"` in prod.tfvars.
Priya: that var was overridden by a PR from last week (ops/infra: change default gpu to A100 for training bench), but the autoscale pools were supposed to pin to a10 via `node_pool_gpu_override`. Looks like the override didn't apply to the spot pool.
Jamal: Billing impact math quick calc: launched 24 nodes * 4 GPU each * 10 hours * A100 list price ~ $3/hr -> ~ $28.8k extra. Rough.
cloud-cost-bot: NOTE: projected additional cost this billing window if pool remains at current size: ~$31.2k.
Ogden: I'm cordoning new nodes, draining non-live pods, and reducing target size to current running replicas to stop further launches. Doing `gcloud` now.
Ogden: ```gcloud compute instance-groups managed set-autoscaling gpu-spot-group --max-num-replicas=2 --zone=us-west1-b```
Alex: thanks. Can someone confirm there are no long-running training jobs pinned to A100 in that pool?
Emily: checked job scheduler logs: no long-running training started in that window. Most were short eval jobs — they were scheduled to the wrong node pool because taints/tolerations mismatched.
Priya: root cause: terraform var override for `gpu_type` applied globally rather than per-pool; module expects `node_pool_gpu_override` but the spot pools didn't include the override. Also training team had an ephemeral change to defaults.
Jamal: opened billing query ticket and added a filter on resource labels for `instance_template` to find all pools impacted. Ticket: BI-3789.
Emily: quick mitigation: patch the autoscaler module to read `local.gpu_type = lookup(var.pool_overrides, var.pool_name, var.gpu_type)` and re-deploy. I'll open a PR and tag @Ogden for review.
Alex: Finance — do we have any reserved commitments that could absorb some of this cost (eg committed use discounts) or is this pure on-demand/spot billing? @Finance-Bot
Finance-Bot: Current datapoint: this is on-demand / spot GPU hours; no committed GPU SKUs covering A100 in us-west1. Reserved commitments apply to vCPU/RAM in certain SKUs only. I'll attach a cost breakdown to BI-3789.
Ogden: After scale down, cluster CPU/GPU headroom looks OK. Killed 18 nodes. Current GPU-hour rate returned to baseline.
Priya: action items: 1) Emergency patch to autoscaler module (Emily) 2) Reconcile billing + request credit (Jamal + Finance) 3) Add CI check to prevent global var overrides for gpu_type (Alex) 4) Postmortem + rollout checklist (Emily + Ogden).
Jamal: For the billing request, we should capture the exact instance ids and timestamps so we can ask cloud support for a good-faith adjustment. I'll export detailed usage and attach.
Emily: PR is up: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/merge_requests/4123 — sets per-pool gpu_type and adds tfplan check.
Alex: Great. Can we add an autoscaler unit test to validate that spot pools default to `A10G`?
Ogden: yes, will add a test and a monitor to alert when `instance_template` accelerator != expected mapping.
Priya: also note: this exposes that our reserved capacity planning table doesn't include GPU family mismatches. We should add a column for `gpu_family` and map commitments to families.
Finance-Bot: Logged cost impact to project BI-3789: approx $29k additional, awaiting detailed export.
Alex: ok — moving to actions. thanks all :thumbsup:
